lines.name: Bakerloo line
lines.description: Opened 1906 as the Baker Street & Waterloo Railway. North of Queen's Park it shares the Watford DC line with the Lioness line; Bakerloo trains ran on to Watford Junction 1917-1982. Extension: Elephant & Castle – Lewisham is planned (route safeguarded 2021, in the Mayor's Transport Strategy; no TWAO or funding; consultation Dec 2026 – Feb 2027; TfL target 2040, slipped from 2028/29). A second phase over the Hayes line is only a possibility (proposed).

lines.description: Opened 1900 as the Central London Railway (Shepherd's Bush – Bank). The eastern branches (Epping, Hainault loop) and the West Ruislip branch were added in 1946-1949 under the New Works Programme, mostly over former main-line railways.

lines.name: Circle line
lines.description: The Inner Circle service of the Metropolitan and District railways began when the loop was completed in 1884; shown as a separate line from 1949. Since December 2009 it runs as a "tea cup": Hammersmith – Edgware Road, then once round the loop back to Edgware Road. It shares all of its track with the Metropolitan, District and Hammersmith & City lines (sections 1863-1884).

lines.description: Paddington – Farringdon is the original Metropolitan Railway of 10 January 1863, the world's first underground railway. The Hammersmith & City Railway opened in 1864; shown as a separate line since 1990.

lines.name: Metropolitan line
lines.description: The Metropolitan Railway opened Paddington – Farringdon on 10 January 1863, the world's first underground railway, and later built out into "Metro-land" towards Buckinghamshire. The Croxley Rail Link (Croxley – Watford Junction via Watford Vicarage Road) had a TWAO in 2013 and some enabling works, but was suspended for lack of funding in 2018 (proposed).

lines.name: Northern line
lines.description: Stockwell – Borough is the City & South London Railway (1890), the world's first deep-level electric tube. The Charing Cross branch began as the Hampstead tube (1907); the two were joined in 1924-1926 and named the Northern line in 1937. High Barnet and Mill Hill East are former main-line branches taken over in 1940-1941. Battersea extension opened in 2021. The official TfL colour is black (#000000); it is drawn dark grey here so that it shows on the dark basemap. Splitting the line into separate Bank and Charing Cross lines is an unfunded TfL aspiration (proposed, possibly 2040s); it adds no track, so it is not drawn.

lines.name: Elizabeth line
lines.description: Crossrail. TfL Rail took over the Shenfield (2015), Heathrow (2018) and Reading (2019) services; the central tunnel Paddington – Abbey Wood opened on 24 May 2022 and through services began in November 2022. The outer sections run on Great Western (1838-1840) and Great Eastern (1839-1843) main lines. New Elizabeth line platforms at Old Oak Common (between Paddington and Acton Main Line) are under construction with HS2; no separate opening date. An extension from Abbey Wood to Dartford / Ebbsfleet (C2E) is proposed: the corridor is safeguarded but DfT has "no plans" for it (2026).

lines.name: Docklands Light Railway
lines.description: Driverless light metro, opened on 31 August 1987 (Tower Gateway / Stratford – Island Gardens) and extended to Bank (1991), Beckton (1994), Lewisham (1999), King George V (2005), Woolwich Arsenal (2009) and Stratford International (2011). Extension Gallions Reach – Beckton Riverside – Thamesmead is planned: Government backed it in the November 2025 Budget, but there is no funding agreement and the TWAO application is due in early 2027 (construction from 2029, opening "early 2030s", no official year).

lines.name: Liberty line
lines.description: Romford – Upminster shuttle (railway 1893), London Overground since 2015. Named Liberty in 2024 after the historic freedoms of Havering.

lines.name: Lioness line
lines.description: Watford DC line Euston – Watford Junction (built 1912-1922), London Overground since November 2007. Shares Queen's Park – Harrow & Wealdstone with the Bakerloo line. Named in 2024 after England's women footballers.

lines.name: Mildmay line
lines.description: North London line Stratford – Richmond and West London line Willesden Junction – Clapham Junction (railways of 1850-1869), London Overground since November 2007. Named in 2024 after the Mildmay Mission Hospital.

segments.label: West London line

lines.name: Suffragette line
lines.description: Gospel Oak – Barking ("GOBLIN", railways of 1868-1894), London Overground since 2007; extended to Barking Riverside on 18 July 2022. Named in 2024 after the suffragette movement.

segments.label: Barking Riverside extension (2022)

lines.name: Weaver line
lines.description: Lea Valley lines from Liverpool Street to Enfield Town, Cheshunt and Chingford (railways of 1840-1891), London Overground since May 2015. Named in 2024 after the area's textile trade.

lines.name: Windrush line
lines.description: East London line. The core through the Thames Tunnel (East London Railway, 1869-1876) was part of the Underground from 1884 (Metropolitan East London line) until 2007; it reopened as London Overground in 2010 with new extensions north to Dalston (Highbury & Islington 2011) and south to Crystal Palace and West Croydon, and the link to Clapham Junction in 2012. Named in 2024 after the Windrush generation.

lines.name: London Trams
lines.description: Tramlink opened in May 2000, partly on former railway alignments (Wimbledon – West Croydon, the Elmers End and Beckenham Junction branches). Central Croydon is a one-way loop. The Sutton Link (Colliers Wood – Sutton) was shelved by TfL in September 2023 for lack of funding (proposed).

lines.name: London Cable Car
lines.description: Aerial cable car (1 km) across the Thames between Greenwich Peninsula and Royal Docks, opened in June 2012 as the Emirates Air Line, IFS Cloud Cable Car 2022-2026, London Cable Car since the sponsorship ended in March 2026. Included because TfL runs it and draws it on its rail maps; it is not a railway (the data format has no cable-car mode, so none is set).

lines.name: Crossrail 2
lines.description: Wimbledon – central London – Dalston, branching to Tottenham Hale (for Broxbourne) and New Southgate, with regional branches beyond Wimbledon (not drawn). Paused since November 2020 as a condition of TfL emergency funding; the route is still safeguarded (2015 directions). Only passive provision is being built (a shaft in the British Library extension, ~2026-2032). Proposed, no year. No official colour (grey chosen for the map). Core stations from the 2015 safeguarding; positions approximate.

lines.name: West London Orbital
lines.description: New London Overground service Hendon – Brent Cross West – Old Oak – Brentford – Hounslow (about 18.5 km) over the Dudding Hill freight line, the North London line and the Hounslow loop. In the London Plan and the Mayor's Transport Strategy; boroughs and TfL funded design to 2028, first consultation open until 18 November 2026; not approved or funded for construction. No official year ("mid-2030s" in the press). The West Hampstead branch has been dropped. Colour: Overground orange (no line colour yet). New stations (Neasden, Harlesden, Old Oak Common Lane, Lionel Road) are approximate.

segments.label: Hendon – Hounslow (planned; consultation 2026; no official year)

lines.name: High Speed 2
lines.description: High-speed line London Euston – Old Oak Common – Birmingham. Under construction: Old Oak Common station (HS2 platforms built, fit-out under way, with new Elizabeth line / GWR platforms), the Euston – Old Oak Common tunnels (boring since January 2026) and the route west via the Northolt tunnels and the Colne Valley Viaduct (complete 2025). Euston station has enabling works only and is not fully funded. 19 May 2026 reset: first services Old Oak Common – Birmingham between May 2036 and October 2039, Euston between May 2040 and December 2043 (the map uses the end of each window). Only the London stations are drawn; the line continues beyond the map. No official map colour (chosen).

notes: Geometry and station positions © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL (route relations fetched via Overpass, simplified ~15 m). Opening years are per section: the year this line (or its predecessor company in today's Underground / TfL network) first carried passengers there. Older main-line tracks that were taken over later carry the takeover year, with the track's own year in the segment label (Central line Epping branch 1949, Elizabeth line Shenfield 2015, Overground 2007-2015). The timeline starts with the Metropolitan Railway (1863). Interchanges are merged when stations share a name within ~450 m, so Paddington, Edgware Road and Hammersmith (two TfL stations each) are one station here, and King's Cross and St Pancras are one. Differently named out-of-station interchanges stay separate: Bank / Monument, Canary Wharf / Heron Quays, Euston / Euston Square, Shepherd's Bush / Shepherd's Bush Market, Woolwich / Woolwich Arsenal, Stratford / Stratford International. Overground line colours follow the 2024 line names (TfL print swatches). Future projects are drawn with approximate stations (approx) and straight lines; see research/london.md for statuses and sources.
